tasks.title: The check ledger: identity, duration, class and unique catches per check per run
tasks.summary: Spec D6, AC8. A pure, read-only fold over gate, queue, integration and revert events that classifies each failure as real, flaky, env or not-run, marks unique catches, severity and sensitive-path guards (failing closed on unknown tasks), and computes runs, minutes, flake rate, importance and merges per post-merge run.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/checkLedger.ts exporting `checkLedger(inputs, opts)`, a pure fold plus an injected tree-diff reader, and named constants `LEDGER_WINDOW_DAYS = 30` and `SEVERITY_WEIGHTS` (S1 8, S2 4, S3 2, S4 1), each commented with spec D6 as its source. `inputs` is task-13's `{events, taskIdOf, taskClaims, sensitiveGlobs}` (this module reads no file). Every task join goes through `taskIdOf` (event id -> qualified task id or `unattributed`). Run rows come from `testgate-result`, the queue's landing and blocked events (task-4's `pre_landing` and per-check fields), `integration-check` records (task-5's fields; probes are runs) and `wave-reverted`. Each row: identity (name plus `cmd_sha256`, or `name-only`), qualified task or epic, tiers, tree, outcome, duration from bs-gate-bounce's `environment.monotonic_ms` (absent -> `null`, never 0), class, unique or shadowed, severity, event id. Classes, unique catch, severity and the sensitive-path guard follow spec D6 exactly: a not-run result (task-1's `isNotRun`, or a name in a record's `not_run`) is counted only as `not_run`; a task that is `unattributed` or has no claims entry counts as touching a sensitive path; severity and the guard otherwise use security.ts `claimTouchesGlob` over the task's claims and `sensitiveGlobs`. The tree-diff reader defaults to `git diff --name-only --no-renames <a> <b>`; an unreadable diff makes the failure `real`. `name-only` rows count toward catches and guards, never runs or minutes. `opts.window` (`{from, to}`) applies to the numbers only; the sensitive-path guard's catch arm reads every event in `inputs`, however old (spec D6). Per identity over the window: runs, measured minutes, unmeasured and not-run counts, median minutes, flake rate, importance, real catches, S1/S2 catches in the window, guards-sensitive, and the event ids behind each number; and the D7 inputs R and M split by source (gate, queue, close). Project-wide: post-merge head runs (`--final` included), task merges, epics with merges, and merges per post-merge run.
acceptance_criteria: test/checkLedger.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), fixtures from test/helpers/ledgerEvents.ts: env (gap at `SLEEP_GAP_MS`), flaky (same identity, same tree, a fail and a pass, as the D4 head re-run writes), real (fail at tree A, pass at tree B, diff touching `src/x.ts`), not-real (fail at A, pass at B, diff touching only the checks file) and not-run (`reason: heavy.wait-timeout`). Each gets a different class, and the test asserts the class strings, so swapping any two definitions fails it.

Not-run: a check whose only failures are lock-wait timeouts has zero runs, zero minutes, zero catches and a `not_run` count equal to the timeouts; a bisect probe listing it in `not_run` adds nothing else.

Unique catch: C fails after faster F passed in the same run -> unique; C fails with faster F ordered after it (short-circuited) -> `shadowed`; F observed passing at the same tree in another record -> unique.

Severity and guard: a catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` is S1 and marks the check guarding; a check with 0 failures that ran on that task's gate inside the window is guarding too; outside the window with no catch it is not. A gate event whose `taskIdOf` entry is `unattributed`, or whose task has no claims entry, marks the check guarding (fail closed).
Identity: two rows with the same name and different `cmd_sha256` are two identities; a `name-only` real catch counts toward the guard but adds no run or minute.
A run with no `environment` has duration `null`; minutes sum measured runs only, with the unmeasured count beside them. An unreadable tree diff (injected reader throws) yields `real`.
Every number names its event ids; the fold writes nothing (inputs deep-equal before and after).

Window: a real catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` 40 days before `now`, with a 30-day window, still marks the check guarding (and task-9 then proposes nothing for it), while that catch adds nothing to the in-window runs, minutes, real catches or S1/S2 catches. A run on that task 40 days ago with no failure does not mark it guarding.

Diff check (AC13), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff --no-renames <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (for example a `timeout_ms` line that only validates or passes through an existing value). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

Flaky is observed (same identity, same tree, both outcomes), never inferred from load or timing; a check that never ran is no evidence of anything.

tasks.summary: Spec D6, AC8. Every task join goes through `taskIdOf` (event id -> qualified task id or `unattributed`). Run rows come from `testgate-result`, task-4's `queue-tier-run` records (one per queue tier run, `results` and `environment` side by side, `task_ids` naming the candidate; the landing and blocked events link a task to its run through `pre_landing_run_id`, and add no run of their own; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-aabfcf57), `integration-check` records (task-5's fields; probes are runs) and `wave-reverted`. Classes, unique catch, severity and the sensitive-path guard follow spec D6 exactly. The class vocabulary is five strings, exported as `FAILURE_CLASSES = ['not-run', 'env', 'flaky', 'real', 'unconfirmed']` and decided in that order: `unconfirmed` is a failure that ran and is none of not-run, env, flaky or real (no later pass of its identity at a different tree for the same task whose diff touches a path other than the checks file, and no confirmed revert of its culprit); it counts as a run with its minutes, and never as a catch or flaky evidence: it adds nothing to real catches, unique catches, importance or flake rate (spec D6; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3661495f). It protects the check as a real catch does, because a failure the ledger can confirm neither way is unverifiable, and D6 lets an unverifiable failure protect a check, never expose it (as an unreadable diff counts as real): per identity the ledger reports unconfirmed failures in the window, each with its event id and its D6 severity (S1 on a task that touches a sensitive path, fail closed as above, else S2: the rule a real catch uses), and the sensitive-path guard's catch arm counts an unconfirmed failure on such a task, however old, as it counts a real catch (spec D6, D7; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac). Further: a not-run result (task-1's `isNotRun`, or a name in a record's `not_run`) is counted only as `not_run`; a task that is `unattributed` or has no claims entry counts as touching a sensitive path; severity and the guard otherwise use security.ts `claimTouchesGlob` over the task's claims and `sensitiveGlobs`. An `unconfirmed` failure adds a run and its minutes and no real catch, unique catch or importance (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-3661495f); it counts in the identity's unconfirmed failures in the window with severity S2, or S1 when its task claims `src/auth/session.ts`, and an S1 unconfirmed failure 40 days before `now` still marks the check guarding, as criterion 8's real catch does (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac).

Unique catch: C fails after faster F passed in the same run -> unique; C fails with faster F ordered after it (short-circuited) -> `shadowed`; F observed passing at the same tree in another record -> unique.

Severity and guard: a catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` is S1 and marks the check guarding; a check with 0 failures that ran on that task's gate inside the window is guarding too; outside the window with no catch it is not. A gate event whose `taskIdOf` entry is `unattributed`, or whose task has no claims entry, marks the check guarding (fail closed).

A run with no `environment` array, with an entry whose `name` differs from its result's, or with `window: 'none'` has duration `null`; minutes sum measured runs only, with the unmeasured count beside them. An event in the shape no writer on the base produces (an `environment` object inside each result and no array beside `results`) yields duration `null` and no env class, so a fixture in that shape cannot pass the duration or env assertions. An unreadable tree diff (injected reader throws) yields `real` (answers f-bs-check-tiers/integration-5d4a0377).
Every number names its event ids; the fold writes nothing (inputs deep-equal before and after).

Window: a real catch on a task claiming `src/auth/session.ts` 40 days before `now`, with a 30-day window, still marks the check guarding (and task-9 then proposes nothing for it), while that catch adds nothing to the in-window runs, minutes, real catches or S1/S2 catches. A run on that task 40 days ago with no failure does not mark it guarding.

tasks.summary: Spec D7-D9, AC9, AC10. A read-only pending fold over undeclared entries with D7's minutes-saved formula per option, notices for declared entries, one validator shared by proposals and apply, an apply that writes the overlay and decision events only, a 90-day quiet decline, and automatic promotion of an overlay-demoted check.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/tierProposals.ts with module-level event-name constants `CHECK_TIER_DECIDED_EVENT`, `CHECK_TIER_PROMOTED_EVENT` and `CHECK_TIER_BATCH_ANSWERED_EVENT`, each written through an `event_type:` property in this file (apply's two appends; the `pending_event` `{event_type: CHECK_TIER_PROMOTED_EVENT, payload}` that promotion stores and then appends), so test/eventTypes.test.ts's scan sees all three written here; and named constants `MIN_RUNS = 20`, `MIN_MEASURED_MINUTES = 30`, `DECLINE_QUIET_DAYS = 90` (commented with spec D7 as their source). Export `pendingProposals(ledger, events, effectiveChecks, overlay, {epicId, writable, now})`, a pure fold that reads only its arguments (no `dir`, no git command, no file): `overlay` is task-15's `readOverlay` result, `writable` is task-15's `overlayWritable(dir)` result (`ok` or the reason) and `epicId` the epic whose lineage `answered_in_epic` reads, both computed by the caller (task-10's `bs checks proposals` from `--project` and `--epic`). It returns demote items exactly as spec D7 defines them (only entries with `tierSource` `default` or `overlay`), in the D7 proposal shape, with `options` computed by D7's formula from the ledger's R, M, d and project-wide B and E (`basis` names each input and whether it was measured or estimated; probes and not-run excluded; minutes rounded to 0.1); `notices` for declared entries (for example a declared post-merge check with a real catch); and task-15's overlay report. Stage-bound checks (gate.ts `stageBoundCheckNames`) are never proposed. Each item also carries task-8's `importance`; items are ordered by post-merge `minutes_saved`, largest first, then by `check`; and the result carries `answered_in_epic` (true when the lineage of `epicId` in `events` holds a `check-tier-batch-answered`). Export `validateDecisions(json, pending)` for the D7 decisions.json shape, and one `itemBlocker(item, ledger, effectiveChecks, now)` used by both `pendingProposals` (to exclude) and apply (to refuse). An unconfirmed failure (task-8's fifth class) protects as a real catch does: `itemBlocker` blocks an item whose check has any unconfirmed failure in the window, whatever its severity, just as D7's zero-real-catches rule blocks one with a real catch, under its own reason `an unconfirmed failure in the window` (it is not reported as an S1 or S2 catch, since it is no catch); and the sensitive-path guard `itemBlocker` reads already counts unconfirmed failures in its catch arm (task-8) (spec D6, D7; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac). `pendingProposals` returns no items, only a notice naming the reason, when `writable` is not `ok` or the ledger is `degraded` (spec D6, D8), so the batch never asks what apply would refuse. Export `applyTierDecisions(decisions, {dir, checksFile, effectiveChecks, actor, ledger, events, now}, ctx, opts)`: with task-15's `overlayPath(dir)` null it refuses `checks.overlay-not-a-repo` without locking or creating anything; a non-operator actor, or a decisions value that is not an array, is refused next with `items: []`, also before the lock, so nothing is created or repaired (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-55ecfc3c); otherwise, inside task-15's `withOverlayLock` (passing no `waitMs`, so task-15's default wait applies; a busy lock is the `checks.overlay-busy` refusal with `items: []`), first `reconcileOverlay`, then validate the whole array with `validateDecisions`, `itemBlocker` and `overlayWritable` against the repaired overlay, and refuse on any failure. Validation checks every item before it refuses. The refusal carries `items`, every failing item as `{proposal_id, check, reason}`, for an item's own causes: a shape error in the item, a check not in the file, a declared tier, a stage-bound check, a sensitive-path guard, an S1 or S2 catch in the window, an unconfirmed failure in the window. It carries `items: []` when the cause is the call's own: a non-operator actor, a decisions value that is not an array, an unwritable overlay, the lock held by a live writer (`checks.overlay-busy`), a failed repair. run.md step 12 reads `items` to re-run apply once without them (task-11; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b12b69b2). One rule for a refusal (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329): it appends none of this batch's events (no `check-tier-decided` and no `check-tier-batch-answered`) and writes none of this batch's decisions to the overlay. The only changes a refused call may leave are two. First, `reconcileOverlay`'s repair of what was already owed before the call (task-15's `overlayOwes`): the overlay entries of approved `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` events already in the log, and the append, exactly as stored, of a `pending_event` the overlay already held. Second, the `.blacksmith/` directory the lock creates when it is absent (task-15; git tracks no empty directory, and no lock file stays). On a consistent overlay, where `overlayOwes` is empty, a refusal therefore leaves the log and the overlay byte-identical. A repair that itself fails (a task-15 `writeOverlay` refusal) refuses the whole call under that code, and the same rule holds. tasks.title: Post-merge resume: every landed bs revert ends with one record, bounce or record-only
tasks.summary: Spec D4, AC6. Scans the integration branch from its fork point for bs revert commits with no `wave-reverted`, validates their trailers, and finishes each: a bounce when the task is still completed and not re-merged, a record-only event with a listed reason otherwise, always accepted; no outcome repeats.
tasks.objective: New module factory/orchestrator/src/postMergeResume.ts exporting `resumeLandedReverts(input, ctx, opts)`. Input: project dir, epic id, the integration branch from task-7's `assertIntegrationBranch`, the epic's event lineage, and `liveTaskIds` (task-12 passes them: the live plan's records whose `task_status` is not `superseded`). For each commit task-7's `landedBsReverts` returns (fork point to head, oldest first) with no `wave-reverted` naming its sha: validate the trailers per spec D4 (`Bs-Revert-Of` 40-hex and a merge commit on the branch's first-parent history; `Bs-Task` a task id of this epic, qualified or bare, qualified with taskId.ts; `Bs-Red-Record` an event id `parseEventId` accepts; `Bs-Failing-Checks` a non-empty comma list). Invalid trailers -> `record-only` with reason `invalid-trailers`; a task id the lineage does not know -> `unknown-task`. Otherwise call task-2's `waveRevertBlocker` with `revertSha`, a git `isAncestor` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) and `liveTaskIds`: null -> `recordWaveReverted` with `disposition: bounce`, `resumed: true`, `failing_checks` from the trailer, the log tail and evidence ids from the red record when it can be read (`evidence: 'record'`), else the trailer's checks and the red record id only (`evidence: 'trailers-only'`); a reason -> `record-only` with that reason and whatever evidence can be read (`evidence: 'unreadable'` with empty lists when none). Each write whose trailers are valid and whose task is known and merged (every reason except `invalid-trailers`, `unknown-task` and `not-merged`) also yields `culprit`, rebuilt from the trailers in task-12's shape: `{task: <Bs-Task, qualified>, merge_sha: <Bs-Revert-Of>, failing_checks: <Bs-Failing-Checks>, red_record_event_id: <Bs-Red-Record>, reproduced: true}`. `reproduced: true` holds because task-12 builds a bs revert commit only after task-7 returned `culprit-found` (spec D4); whether each check's own failure was env or not-run is read later from the red record by task-9's promotion, never assumed here. Return `{outcome, resumed, wrote: [{task, revert_sha, disposition, reason?, culprit?}]}`: outcome `reverted` with `resumed: true` when every write was a bounce, `revert-recorded` when any was record-only, `nothing-to-resume` (`resumed: false`) when none was missing. It never moves a ref. Its fixtures are built inside test/postMergeResume.test.ts with the repo builder task-7 exports from test/helpers/integrationRepo.ts (imported, not edited).
acceptance_criteria: test/postMergeResume.test.ts (write first; fails today because the module does not exist), with a bs revert commit landed and no `wave-reverted`: the task still completed -> one `wave-reverted` with `disposition: bounce`, return `{outcome: 'reverted', resumed: true}`, and the task folds to `todo`.

One fixture per record-only exit, each writing exactly one `record-only` event with the named reason, returning `revert-recorded`, and leaving the task's folded status unchanged: superseded after the revert; waived; escalated (`held-by-operator`); merged again after the revert, by a `wave-merged` whose `merge_sha` has R as an ancestor (`re-merged`); a `Bs-Task` naming no known task (`unknown-task`); a `Bs-Task` naming a task the lineage knows (its `wave-admitted`) with no `wave-merged` (`not-merged`); a task merged and still completed that a later plan amendment dropped, so `liveTaskIds` lacks it (`not-in-live-plan`); a `Bs-Revert-Of` that is not 40-hex (`invalid-trailers`). Every bad trailer value is written through the trailer parameters of task-7's builder, never by a hand-made commit.

The integration ref and the clone's branch, index and tree are byte-identical before and after every fixture.

Export `pendingProposals(ledger, events, effectiveChecks, overlay, {epicId, writable, now})`, a pure fold that reads only its arguments (no `dir`, no git command, no file): `overlay` is task-15's `readOverlay` result, `writable` is task-15's `overlayWritable(dir)` result (`ok` or the reason) and `epicId` the epic whose lineage `answered_in_epic` reads, both computed by the caller (task-10's `bs checks proposals` from `--project` and `--epic`). It returns demote items exactly as spec D7 defines them (only entries with `tierSource` `default` or `overlay`), in the D7 proposal shape, with `options` computed by D7's formula from the ledger's R, M, d and project-wide B and E (`basis` names each input and whether it was measured or estimated; probes and not-run excluded; minutes rounded to 0.1); `notices` for declared entries (for example a declared post-merge check with a real catch); and task-15's overlay report. Stage-bound checks (gate.ts `stageBoundCheckNames`) are never proposed. Each item also carries task-8's `importance`; items are ordered by post-merge `minutes_saved`, largest first, then by `check`; and the result carries `answered_in_epic` (true when the lineage of `epicId` in `events` holds a `check-tier-batch-answered`). Export `validateDecisions(json, pending)` for the D7 decisions.json shape, and one `itemBlocker(item, ledger, effectiveChecks, now)` used by both `pendingProposals` (to exclude) and apply (to refuse). An unconfirmed failure (task-8's fifth class) protects as a real catch does: `itemBlocker` blocks an item whose check has any unconfirmed failure in the window, whatever its severity, just as D7's zero-real-catches rule blocks one with a real catch, under its own reason `an unconfirmed failure in the window` (it is not reported as an S1 or S2 catch, since it is no catch); and the sensitive-path guard `itemBlocker` reads already counts unconfirmed failures in its catch arm (task-8) (spec D6, D7; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-c9adc1ac). `pendingProposals` returns no items, only a notice naming the reason, when `writable` is not `ok` or the ledger is `degraded` (spec D6, D8), so the batch never asks what apply would refuse. Export `applyTierDecisions(decisions, {dir, checksFile, effectiveChecks, actor, ledger, events, now}, ctx, opts)`: with task-15's `overlayPath(dir)` null it refuses `checks.overlay-not-a-repo` without locking or creating anything; a non-operator actor, or a decisions value that is not an array, is refused next with `items: []`, also before the lock, so nothing is created or repaired (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-55ecfc3c); otherwise, inside task-15's `withOverlayLock` (passing no `waitMs`, so task-15's default wait applies; a busy lock is the `checks.overlay-busy` refusal with `items: []`), first `reconcileOverlay`, then validate the whole array with `validateDecisions`, `itemBlocker` and `overlayWritable` against the repaired overlay, and refuse on any failure. Validation checks every item before it refuses. The refusal carries `items`, every failing item as `{proposal_id, check, reason}`, for an item's own causes: a shape error in the item, a check not in the file, a declared tier, a stage-bound check, a sensitive-path guard, an S1 or S2 catch in the window, an unconfirmed failure in the window. It carries `items: []` when the cause is the call's own: a non-operator actor, a decisions value that is not an array, an unwritable overlay, the lock held by a live writer (`checks.overlay-busy`), a failed repair. run.md step 12 reads `items` to re-run apply once without them (task-11; f-bs-check-tiers/integration-b12b69b2). One rule for a refusal (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329): it appends none of this batch's events (no `check-tier-decided` and no `check-tier-batch-answered`) and writes none of this batch's decisions to the overlay. The only changes a refused call may leave are two. First, `reconcileOverlay`'s repair of what was already owed before the call (task-15's `overlayOwes`): the overlay entries of approved `check-tier-decided` and `check-tier-promoted` events already in the log, and the append, exactly as stored, of a `pending_event` the overlay already held. Second, the `.blacksmith/` directory the lock creates when it is absent (task-15; git tracks no empty directory, and no lock file stays). On a consistent overlay, where `overlayOwes` is empty, a refusal therefore leaves the log and the overlay byte-identical. A repair that itself fails (a task-15 `writeOverlay` refusal) refuses the whole call under that code, and the same rule holds. A call that takes the lock reconciles before it validates, so its batch is judged against the tiers the log already decided, and a crash converges on the next call that takes the lock, whatever that call's batch holds (spec D8). A call refused before it takes the lock (`checks.overlay-not-a-repo`, a non-operator actor, a decisions value that is not an array, or a lock still busy when the wait ends, `checks.overlay-busy`) runs no reconcile and repairs nothing; the repair waits for the next call that takes the lock (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-bd5b4ed3). Every call that is not refused, an empty array included, finally appends one `check-tier-batch-answered` (`epic_id`, decided ids, pending ids) for the epic it is given, so a reply of `none` or an unparseable one is recorded and not asked again in that epic; a refused call appends none, so `answered_in_epic` stays false (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-0cb51329). It appends exactly one `check-tier-batch-answered` with `decided: []`, `pending` (the ids `pendingProposals` returns), and `handed_off: {code, decisions_path}`. It validates nothing of the reply, takes no lock and writes no overlay, so it decides nothing and every item stays pending. That event is the durable record that the batch was asked: the same fold that sets `answered_in_epic` reads it, so no later entry to step 12 asks again. The operator ends the hand-off by running an accepted `bs checks apply` with that decisions.json (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-852a2111). `pendingProposals` reads every `check-tier-batch-answered` of the epic's lineage alike for `answered_in_epic`. It also reports `handed_off`: the latest hand-off's `{code, decisions_path, event_id}` when no `check-tier-batch-answered` without `handed_off` follows it in that lineage, else null. The project's checks file is never opened for writing. Export `promoteAfterCatch(...)` for D7's automatic promotion: its evidence is a post-merge culprit result from task-7 (`{failing_checks, red_record_event_id, reproduced: true}`, spec D7), not the ledger. It returns one answer per entry of the culprit's `failing_checks`, in that order, each `{check, result, reason}`; every case below is an answer, never a throw (f-bs-check-tiers/integration-e4d115dc). Each check gets the answer of the first rule that applies. (a) The red record named by `red_record_event_id` is not in the events it is given (a resumed culprit whose record was lost), or holds no result with that check's name -> `result: 'promotion-skipped'`, `reason: 'red-record-unreadable'`. (b) The check declares its tier -> `declared-tier-wins`. (c) Its effective tier, from task-15's `resolveEffectiveTiers` over an unlocked `readOverlay(dir)`, does not have `tierSource: 'overlay'` from an approved `check-tier-decided` -> `not-promoted`, `reason: 'not-demoted'`; outside a git repository no check has an overlay tier, so every undeclared one ends here and the lock is never reached. (d) Its own failure in that record was not-run (task-1's `isNotRun`, or its name in the record's `not_run`) -> `not-promoted`, `reason: 'not-run'`; or env (`sleptDuringCheck` on the record's `environment` entry at that result's index, the per-check rule task-7 step (6) and task-8 use) -> `not-promoted`, `reason: 'env-failure'`. (e) Otherwise it promotes: inside `withOverlayLock` (passing no `waitMs`, so task-15's default wait applies), after `reconcileOverlay`, it writes the overlay entry as `pre-merge` with `pending_event` holding the `check-tier-promoted` payload (`check`, `cmd_sha256`, `from_tier`, `to_tier: pre-merge`, `catch_event_id`, `decided_by_event_id`), then appends that event and clears `pending_event` -> `promoted`. Answers (a) to (d) are decided from the arguments and an unlocked `readOverlay` before the lock, so they take no lock, run no reconcile and change nothing on disk; only (e) takes the lock. task-14 prints these answers, and task-11 reports the `promotion-skipped` and `declared-tier-wins` ones.
